per_question.question: What DME items are specifically NOT covered by NC Medicaid under the Orthotics and Prosthetics policy, and what general criteria must be met for coverage?
per_question.agent_answer:
I found the main NC Medicaid clinical policy: Policy 5B, Orthotics & Prosthetics. The frame points to the general coverage criteria in sections 3.1 and 3.2.1, and the non-covered items in section 4.2. I still need to verify whether Policy 5B has any amendments or change notices before I present it as current, so I’m checking the document record and amendment history next.I confirmed that Policy 5B is the authoritative current document in the corpus, and the amendment lookup did not return any separate change notices. I have enough to answer the core question, but I want to read the full non-covered subsections directly—especially 4.2.1 and 4.2.2, plus 4.1—so I can distinguish general noncoverage rules from the specific list the user asked about.## NC Medicaid Orthotics & Prosthetics: items specifically not covered, and general coverage criteria

Under **NC Medicaid Clinical Coverage Policy 5B, Orthotics & Prosthetics**, the policy lists these **specific categories not covered**:

- **Devices for the beneficiary’s comfort or convenience**, or for the convenience of the beneficiary’s caregiver(s)
- **Backup or duplicate devices** kept on hand or available at different locations
- **Devices and supplies for residents of nursing facilities**
- **Devices or supplies covered by another agency**
- **Equipment or supplies for beneficiaries receiving hospice care**, as described in the policy’s care-coordination section  
  ([Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment), § 4.2.1)

### General noncoverage rules
The same policy also says orthotics/prosthetics are **not covered** if:

- the beneficiary does **not** meet the eligibility requirements in Section 2.0;
- the beneficiary does **not** meet the coverage criteria in Section 3.0;
- the item or service **duplicates another provider’s** procedure, product, or service; or
- the item or service is **experimental, investigational, or part of a clinical trial**  
  ([Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment), § 4.1)

## General criteria that must be met for coverage

### 1) General covered-service criteria
For coverage, the procedure, product, or service must be:

- **individualized, specific, and consistent** with the beneficiary’s symptoms or confirmed diagnosis, and **not more than the beneficiary needs**;
- able to be **safely furnished**, with **no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment available statewide**; and
- furnished in a way **not primarily intended for the convenience** of the beneficiary, caregiver, or provider  
  ([Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment), § 3.1)

### 2) Orthotics/prosthetics-specific coverage criteria
The policy also requires that orthotic/prosthetic items:

- be **ordered by a physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner**;
- be **medically necessary** to maintain or improve the beneficiary’s medical, physical, or functional level, and be appropriate for use in a **noninstitutional setting** where normal life activities occur;
- be supported by a **face-to-face encounter** with the ordering physician, PA, or NP **within 6 months before initiation** of the orthotic/prosthetic item; and
- have the beneficiary’s need **reviewed at least annually** by the ordering physician, PA, or NP  
  ([Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment), § 3.2.1)

The policy further explains:

- **Orthotic devices** are medically necessary when required to **correct or prevent skeletal deformities**, **support or align movable body parts**, or **preserve or improve physical function**.
- **Prosthetic devices** are medically necessary when replacing all or part of the function of a **permanently inoperative, absent, or malfunctioning body part**, and the beneficiary must need the prosthesis for **mobility, daily care, or rehabilitation**.
- Orthotic and prosthetic devices also must be:
  - a **reasonable and medically necessary** part of the treatment plan;
  - **consistent with the beneficiary’s diagnosis and medical condition**, especially the functional limitations and symptoms; and
  - of **high quality**, with replacement parts available  
  ([Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment), § 3.2.1)

## Bottom line
The policy’s **specific “not covered” list** is mostly about items that are for comfort/convenience, duplicates/backups, nursing-facility residents, items covered elsewhere, and hospice-related equipment/supplies. Coverage generally requires **medical necessity, an appropriate order, recent face-to-face evaluation, annual review, and that the item be tailored to the beneficiary’s condition rather than convenience**.

I checked the amendment history in the corpus, and **Policy 5B is the authoritative current document with no separate amendments returned by the amendment tool**. If you want, I can also pull out any **DME-like items within 5B that are limited or excluded by subtype**—for example helmets, orthopedic shoes, elastic supports, or supplies.
